title: Rate limiter: token bucket
summary: Tokens refill with elapsed time, capped at capacity; a request spends one whole token or is refused. The clock is passed in so tests control time. O(1) per request.
code: # Refill by elapsed time up to capacity; a request spends one token or is refused.
triggers: allow at most N requests per period with short bursts, per user or per API key
throttling, quotas and 'too many requests' errors
prompts: A public API lets each key make a burst of ten calls, then roughly one call per second. Calls beyond the allowance get an error instead of waiting.
A game server lets each player fire a few shots in quick succession but limits sustained firing, so scripted clicking gains nothing.
invariant: Before each decision tokens = min(capacity, tokens + elapsed × rate); a request is allowed only when a whole token is available, and it spends that token.
mantra: Refill by elapsed time, cap it, spend one.
pitfalls: Cap the refill at capacity, or an idle client banks an unlimited burst.
Record the refill time on every call, or the same seconds are credited twice.
Inject the clock so tests control time, and keep one bucket per user or key.

anchors.name: API rate limiter
anchors.trick: One bucket per key: burst = capacity, sustained rate = refill.

anchors.name: Logger Rate Limiter
anchors.trick: A simpler rule: remember when each message may print again.

anchors.name: Design Hit Counter
anchors.trick: A sliding window of timestamps instead of tokens.

mutations.explanation: Without the cap, a long idle period banks unlimited tokens and allows a burst far beyond capacity.
Allows a request with only part of a token, so the bucket runs into debt and lets traffic through too early.
